text:
Dylan: Heads-up — saw p95 dip under p50 on the latency dashboard for a handful of endpoints right after the quota failover. Anyone else?
Maya: Yep, spotted at ~08:12. Chart looked like p95 and p50 crossed for /v1/generate and /v1/complete. Felt like a visualization bug.
Lee: I downloaded the raw samples for /v1/generate. The distribution changed post-failover: a bunch of 5-20ms samples appeared that weren't there before. Sample counts didn't drop.
Anya: Is the console merging different routing cohorts? We recently changed failover routing to use a dedicated pool that tends to be lower-latency.
Dylan: Query used by panel (simplified):
```
SELECT quantile(0.5, latency) AS p50, quantile(0.95, latency) AS p95
FROM latency_measurements
WHERE endpoint IN ('/v1/generate','/v1/complete') AND env='prod'
GROUP BY 1m
```
Maya: Toggling "group by" in the UI changes the symptom. If I group by deployment the lines flip; if I group by route-only they're correct.
Lee: Root cause hypothesis: rollup pipeline merges samples from fallback/dedicated pool but drops sample_origin label. Aggregator defaults missing origin to primary cohort, so latency percentiles for primary cohort get contaminated by the low-latency fallback samples.
SRE-Bot: Event: quota-failover executed 2024-09-12T08:11:07Z for tenant-prod; policy=failover->dedicated-pool-2.
Anya: That matches. If origin is omitted during the relabel stage, downstream rollups will incorrectly assume those samples belong to the normal route.
Dylan: I grepped traces: lines like `endpoint=/v1/generate latency=18ms sample_origin=primary` then later `endpoint=/v1/generate latency=6ms` (no origin). Aggregator interprets absent origin as primary by default.
Maya: Which explains why p95 collapsed — low-latency failover samples diluted the main cohort. We ended up paging on a false SLO regression.
Lee: Short-term mitigation: change the rollup merger to treat missing sample_origin as "unknown" and keep it as a separate bucket. That should stop cohort bleed.
Anya: Long-term we should ensure relabelers always emit provenance and plumb the origin tag through the remapper. Also add a compact provenance breakdown in the legend (hover) so product/ops can see percent by origin without drilling.
Dylan: Agreed. I'll open an eng-platform ticket for the relabeler fix and link the incident.
Maya: Also recommend muting the p95 SLO alerts for affected routes until we get the fix out and validated. We paged on bad data this morning.
Lee: I'll push a small change to the rollup merger to map missing -> "unknown" and run it in staging. ETA 30m for canary.
SRE-Bot: Incident created: 2024-09-12 - quota-failover-provenance-leak (https://incidents.local/2024-09-12-001).
Anya: UX mock: hover over latency legend -> shows tiny table: [{origin: primary, count: 1200, pct: 85%}, {origin: dedicated-pool-2, count: 180, pct: 13%}, {origin: unknown, count: 20, pct: 2%}]. Keep it clickable to filter the chart.
Dylan: Nice. That would make it much faster to triage.
Lee: Canary rolled to staging; provenance persists now, p95 > p50 again in the staging view. I'll promote after a short bake.
Maya: I'll mute alerts and monitor. Thanks.
Dylan: Summary/actions: (1) Lee: change rollup to treat missing origin as "unknown" + promote canary (2) Anya: prototype provenance legend hover and filter UX (3) Maya: mute SLO alerts for affected routes and monitor (4) Dylan: open tracker and link incident.
Maya: Looping in @oncall for alert mute. :thumbsup:
Lee: Canary looks healthy in prod after promotion. Charts look normal again.
Dylan: Closing the loop — false-positive paging prevented. Let's follow up next week on adding provenance counts to the console and a postmortem blurb. :tada:
